title: AI Agents Can Delete Files. Here’s How IT Teams Get Them Back.
summary: AI agents have wiped drives and home folders on real machines. Here is how IT teams reduce the risk and restore files with endpoint backup.
body_markdown:
If an AI agent deletes files on a work laptop, you can only restore them if a copy exists somewhere the agent couldn’t reach. That usually means an endpoint backup with version history, stored off the machine. Git, sync folders, and the Recycle Bin often won’t cover it.


The stories keep coming. Someone gives an AI agent access to their computer. It runs a cleanup command. Files disappear. If you manage laptops for your company or for clients, you’ll get that call sooner or later.


## What are people reporting?


These are individual accounts and news reports. Causes vary and some details are unconfirmed. But the pattern shows up across tools and vendors.


- A Cursor forum user[said an agent asked to clone a Git repository ran recursive delete commands and wiped files across the C: drive](https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-agent-completely-wiped-my-c-drive-and-deleted-everything/164675) . He said he had no backup.
- Gigazine[covered a Reddit report that Google’s Antigravity agent deleted the contents of a user’s drive](https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20251205-ai-pc-data-delete) .
- TechRadar[reported that a Claude Code agent deleted about 48,000 files in just over 100 seconds](https://techradar.com/pro/security/i-broke-something-a-claude-code-ai-agent-deleted-48-000-files-in-just-over-100-seconds-then-apologized-for-doing-so) . The report says it mishandled Windows junctions and corrupted the repository’s Git object database.
- The AI Incident Database[logged a report from Matt Shumer that an OpenAI Codex agent deleted most of the files in his Mac home directory during a cleanup task](https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1671/) .


No single vendor owns this problem. An agent runs commands with the same permissions as the person who started it. If the user can delete it, so can the agent.


Most of these reports come from developers. But any employee who runs an agent on a company laptop has the same exposure.


## Why don’t the deleted files show up in the Recycle Bin?


Often the delete command skips it. In the Antigravity report, the command used a quiet flag, so[the files bypassed the Recycle Bin](https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20251205-ai-pc-data-delete) . Terminal deletes on a Mac work the same way. They don’t go to the Trash.


So the first place people look is empty.


## Can Git, OneDrive, or Time Machine get the files back?


Sometimes. Not reliably.


Git only protects what you’ve committed. In the TechRadar case, the Git database itself was damaged. Uncommitted work, local config, and files outside the repo were never covered.


Sync tools like OneDrive and Dropbox mirror changes, and a deletion is a change. Recovery depends on your retention settings, and sync only watches the folders you point it at.


Time Machine or a NAS can work for one person who set it up and keeps the drive connected. Across a fleet, you can’t easily confirm it’s running.


What you want is a copy that lives off the machine, runs on its own and keeps older versions.


## How do you reduce the risk first?


Backup is the last line of defense. Start earlier.


- Run agents in a sandbox or a separate user account, not the main profile.
- Require approval for any command that deletes.
- Keep agents out of home directories and shared drives.
- Make sure people know what a “full access” setting actually allows.


Those steps help. They won’t catch everything. Someone will approve the wrong prompt, or a tool will read a command in a way nobody expected. That’s when you need to restore.


## What should you look for in an endpoint backup?


1. It runs by itself. Users shouldn’t have to start it, and it should cover their main folders by default.
2. Long version history. People often notice missing files days later, not minutes later.
3. Admin control over restores. You decide who can restore what, from one console.
4. Deployment through your MDM or RMM, so rollout doesn’t mean touching every machine.
5. Pricing you can plan around. Per-gigabyte billing turns budgeting into a guess.

## FAQ


### Can you recover files an AI agent deleted?


If a backup ran before the deletion, yes. You restore the files from version history. Without a backup, your options are limited and results aren’t guaranteed.


### Does endpoint backup replace Git?


No. Git tracks code changes and lets teams collaborate. Backup protects the whole machine, including files that never made it into a repo.
